issues.description: Silent semantic change: identity replaced with coerceNumber that maps null/NaN to 0
issues.detail: Original panLinear/zoomLinear used identity as ground, so toNumber(domain[0]) flowed through unchanged. The new coerceNumber coerces null to 0 via `?? 0`. If domain contains a non-numeric value, the old code returned NaN; the new code silently returns 0, hiding bad input. State this invariant in a comment or preserve the prior behavior.

issues.description: Length-1 domain passes isNonEmpty guard but violates the algorithm's two-endpoint invariant
issues.detail: The pan/zoom invariant requires domain[0] and peek(domain) to be distinct endpoints of an interval. isNonEmpty(arr) accepts arr.length === 1, where d0 === d1 and dd === 0, producing a degenerate domain silently. Either tighten the guard to length >= 2 or document why length-1 is acceptable.

issues.description: Domain type `number[]` is wider than the algorithm's actual precondition
issues.detail: The functions return `Domain = [number, number]` but accept `number[]`, then runtime-check non-emptiness. The literate move is to either accept `NonEmptyArray<number>` at the type level (push the check to the caller) or document at the function why the runtime guard exists despite the type. Currently the type and the guard tell different stories.

issues.description: No invariant comment on the pan/zoom helpers
issues.detail: These are the central algorithms of the file, yet neither pan() nor zoom() carries a docstring stating the invariant: given a sorted two-point domain [d0, d1] in scale space, the result is the transformed interval after translating by delta or scaling about anchor. A two-line literate comment above each helper would make the file readable without running it.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new error path is partial
issues.detail: Only panLinear and zoomLinear are tested for the empty-domain throw. panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the same guard via pan/zoom, so one parameterized test per helper would suffice — but the current tests leave six exported functions unverified for the new contract.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The type annotations are a real improvement and the empty-domain guard adds a useful precondition, but two algorithmic concerns went unstated. First, the new coerceNumber wrapper silently maps null to 0 where the old identity preserved whatever toNumber returned — a semantic shift not documented in the diff. Second, isNonEmpty allows length-1 arrays through a guard that exists to ensure two distinct endpoints; the type Domain = [number, number] promises something the runtime check does not enforce. The pan/zoom helpers also lack the one-line invariant comment that would make this file literate. Tests cover only the linear variants of the new throw.
